question.text: A trader purchases a call option on a stock with strike Rs. 500 at a premium of Rs. 25. At expiry, the stock closes at Rs. 480. What is the trader's profit or loss?

explanation.text: The Logic: Call Profit = max(S - X, 0) - Premium. Here S = Rs. 480 and X = Rs. 500. Since S is less than X, the call expires worthless and the loss equals the premium paid. Payoff = max(-20, 0) = 0, so net P/L = 0 - 25 = -Rs. 25. The Trap: The loss is not Rs. 45 (that figure adds the price gap to the premium). Profit of Rs. 20 inverts the position. "No profit, no loss" ignores the fact that the premium is paid up front and not recovered when the option expires OTM.
